newsitem.title: ESTONIA: Estonian central bank approves bank merger.
newsitem.headline: Estonian central bank approves bank merger.

text.p: The Bank of Estonia said on Monday it had approved a merger between Estonia's Savings bank and the Bank of Industry.
"The merger was approved on Monday morning," a central bank spokesman told Reuters.
Savings is the second largest commercial bank in Estonia and the Bank of Industry is the eighth.
The merger was hit by controversy earlier after leading politicians alleged that the Bank of Industry's loan losses were larger than it admitted.
The merger will boost Savings Bank's assets to more than four billion kroons ($335.4 million).
Savings Bank made a profit of 22.4 million kroons in the first half of the year.
The bank also plans to boost its share capital to 143 million kroons with a 10 million kroon share emission.
Analysts consider Estonia's banking sector as the healthiest among Baltic countries. Latvia and Lithuania are still pulling themselves out of banking crises that erupted last year.
Estonia's sector went through a period of turbulence in 1992 when the government took the politically painful decision to allow some troubled banks to go under.
But economists said the government's refusal to bail out troubled banks and strict central bank supervision have paid off and instilled confidence in the sector.
